About matching & export

Signature protection: always on. PDFs with detected digital signatures open in view-only mode. Download returns the original file unchanged. This editor does not verify certificate trust or signature validity.

Font names and sizes come from the PDF. Bold and italic are inferred from font names; underline and paragraph structure are not reliably encoded.

The editor reuses the PDF's embedded font program, so characters used elsewhere in the document are available here too. Subset fonts can still lack characters that never appear; load the full TTF/OTF for those.

Exports preserve native text, graphics and existing images. Edited text stays selectable; pages are never converted to images.

Watermarks and artwork remain in their original PDF structure. Check the export before sharing. Edits can be detected and may invalidate signatures.

Export size depends on the original content and any fonts you add. Previously rasterized PDFs remain images; reopen the original PDF to keep its text.

Sign a new copy

Your certificate and password stay in this browser. Signing adds a record page identifying the new signer. Existing signed PDFs remain protected.

Choose a certificate to see the signing identity.

RSA 2048+ only. Certificate trust and revocation are not checked. Signing time uses your device clock; no trusted timestamp is included.

Encrypt a PDF copy

Choose any unencrypted PDF; this works independently of the document open in the editor. AES-256 password protection is applied in this browser. Existing digital signatures cannot be preserved in a rewritten file, so signed PDFs are refused.

When supplied, only this JSON’s fields become the encrypted PDF’s native Info/XMP metadata: omitted original Info fields and XMP are removed, and the JSON file is not attached. Use the metadata JSON downloaded from this app, a file metadata report such as {"file":{"name":"statement.pdf","sizeBytes":583255,"hashes":{"SHA-256":"…"}},"metadata":{"version":"1.4","pages":15,"Producer":"openhtmltopdf.com","CreationDate":"D:…"}} (stored as native Producer/CreationDate plus Source… custom fields), a flat object such as {"Title":"New title","Author":"Name","Custom":{"Project":"123"}}, or {"info":{"Title":"New title"},"xmp":{"raw":"...XMP XML..."}}. Leave it empty to retain the source PDF’s existing native metadata. PDF structure properties such as page count, encryption and signatures cannot be set from JSON. Info values must be text, a number, a boolean or a PDF name object such as {"name":"False"}; lists are joined for the standard text fields. Nested objects and arrays cannot be stored in PDF Info. In a flat JSON, every top-level key except xmp/XMP and Custom is treated as an Info field, so remove unrelated keys such as file. If a value is unsupported, nothing is downloaded; fix the JSON or use Encrypt without metadata to keep the PDF’s existing metadata. Passwords are not stored or sent anywhere. Use HTTPS or localhost for AES-256.

This preview is embedded in another page, and some browsers block automatic downloads inside embedded frames. After encrypting, if no file appears, use Save again in the download panel or Open app in new tab, then repeat the encryption there.

Metadata JSON can’t be used

PDF Info is a flat dictionary and can only store text, numbers, booleans or PDF names. The JSON file itself is never attached. Without a usable JSON, the encrypted copy keeps the PDF’s existing native Info/XMP metadata.

Source PDF metadata

The Info fields below are native metadata from the opened PDF; calculated properties such as PDF version are excluded. Without a replacement file, edited exports retain its Info/XMP and attach this source record. If you choose a JSON replacement below, its supported fields become the PDF's native Info/XMP metadata instead; no new JSON attachment is added. This record does not validate a signature.

Open a PDF to inspect its metadata.

Use a JSON object such as {"Title":"Updated title","Author":"Name","Custom":{"Project":"123"}}, a metadata JSON downloaded here, or a file metadata report with "file"/"metadata" objects (hashes and structure become Source… custom fields). For XMP, include "xmp":{"raw":"...XML..."}. Only supplied Info/XMP fields remain: missing original fields and XMP are removed. PDF structure (pages, encryption, signatures) cannot be replaced by metadata. This is not a redaction of page-level metadata or existing attachments. The new export has different bytes and hashes, even without text edits. Signed or encrypted PDFs stay view-only.

No metadata replacement loaded. The source PDF’s native Info/XMP is retained.

File fingerprints

SHA-256 and SHA-512 identify exact file bytes. A hash alone does not prove issuer identity. The current export includes applied edits and any uploaded metadata replacement.
